question: When could a frequency-dependent wavelet track add useful attack timing evidence to fixed-window FFT/STFT analysis of the GAS-001 guitar fixture?
production_path: source_review: inspect pinned GAS-001 fixture, measurement script, and saved results alongside AUD-003 and PHY-002
implementation_review: inspect pinned IX STFT and Haar source and pinned GA scalar-series wavelet service
derived_calculation: calculate Morlet-style sigma and nominal plus-or-minus-four-sigma spans for the first, second, and fourth E2 partials
experiment_design: pre-register a synthetic-burst timing comparison with the pinned recorded and rendered guitar fixture as a sensitivity follow-up
evidence_limit: no comparative STFT/Morlet run, saved full Morlet envelope, listening trial, or verified live analyzer
hypothesis: The GAS-001 Morlet-style kernel's time support shrinks with center frequency, so its fourth-partial track may yield lower timing error than a long fixed-window IX STFT on a controlled guitar-like burst; whether that advantage survives a short STFT baseline, frequency-confusion checks, and the recorded GA comparison remains unmeasured.
evidence: At Demerzel commit 5c4967454ddc740ed937c87719ca4d71a3522e4b, state/streeling/fixtures/guitar-acoustics/gas-001/README.md and measure-pair.py pin the source WAVs, approximate onset markers, three Morlet-style centers, sigma=6/(2*pi*f), and radius=ceil(4*sigma*sample_rate). The saved measurements.json reports second-partial late-minus-early changes of -4.5 dB recorded and -12.9 dB render. Its JSON contains peak times and summaries, not the full envelope arrays.

Direct calculation using target 82.4069 Hz and harmonics 1, 2, 4 gives Gaussian sigma 11.588, 5.794, 2.897 ms and nominal full plus-or-minus-four-sigma spans 92.704, 46.352, 23.176 ms. Discrete kernel endpoints differ slightly because measure-pair.py applies ceil to each radius. These are source-derived calculations, not measured localization errors.

At IX commit bd1336b7c4045e427dcdbe80b102790e45da5ce1, crates/ix-signal/src/spectral.rs:6-54 implements fixed-size Hann-windowed STFT/spectrogram and crates/ix-agent/src/handlers.rs:1143-1189 enforces a power-of-two window. Crates/ix-signal/src/wavelet.rs:5-82 implements Haar DWT and denoising, not GAS-001's Morlet-style measurement.

At GA commit dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924, Common/GA.Business.ML/Wavelets/WaveletTransformService.cs decomposes scalar series with Haar or Daubechies-4 and extracts aggregate statistics. Inspection of this class does not show a guitar-audio integration.

The proposed offline benchmark specifies 44100-sample separate trials per center, two 40 ms Hann-gated phase-zero 0.5-peak bursts at 0.30 and 0.45 s, a fixed-seed white-noise arm at RMS 0.01, a clean arm, a plus-or-minus-60 ms peak-picking interval, two IX STFT sizes, and the pinned Morlet-style kernel. STFT tracks use the nearest declared-center bin without interpolation; all method/center tracks are normalized by their median steady-state response to separate clean unit-peak one-second sinusoids before both burst arms are scored. An illustrative 5 ms median fourth-partial timing-error improvement against the longer STFT and at least 6 dB correct-center versus largest calibrated wrong-center peak separation can falsify the limited timing hypothesis. These are teaching thresholds, not project acceptance criteria. This benchmark and the follow-up GAS-001 sensitivity analysis have not been run. Research duration was not instrumented; duration_seconds=0 records that limit.
